items.title: César Azpilicueta: ‘At Chelsea a draw was a catastrophe – if you can’t perform, you’re out’
items.summary: Former defender reflects on his record-breaking longevity, kicking Eden Hazard in training, and life after retirementCésar Azpilicueta looks well. César Azpilicueta always looks well – “ah, Captain Handsome,” one Chelsea fan says when told who’s turning up – but today especially, smiling in the sunshine. Strolling in, he eases into an easier chair, golf course spreading out beyond the terrace, west of Madrid, and orders a detox almost as green. It is nearly 20 years since he played his first game and a few months since he played his last, training kit replaced by bermudas, loafers and a polo, a picture of relaxation. So what’s it like not being a footballer? “Well, different,” he says. Then he laughs, which he does a lot.It is not a laugh-your-head-off laugh, more a chuckle, a giggle, as if amused at everything he did. And for all the self-deprecation, the lack of triumphalism, he did everything. Now, at 37, it’s not the same, although there remains much to do, Azpilicueta as understated and quietly busy as ever: “square,” he calls himself. He’s completed an MBA, a sports directorship diploma and there are media offers, a life to live. Matches to play still: against his kids the needle is never far away, he says. And although he hasn’t found a seven-a-side team yet he will. Continue reading...

items.summary: England face All Blacks rematch in third-place gameIreland take on Australia to decide fifth spotFrance and South Africa will contest the inaugural Nations Championship grand final next Sunday in London, while England will face an immediate rematch with the All Blacks next Saturday.Les Bleus defeated Argentina 45-17 in Paris, ultimately overwhelming the Pumas with five second-half tries and seven overall at the Stade de France. They confirmed top spot in the northern hemisphere table with the required bonus-point win, finishing on 26 points with five wins out of six. England (five bonus points) and Ireland (four bonus points) also won five matches, but finish second and third respectively. Continue reading...

items.title: Teenage ace Williams-Barnett puts Tottenham on path to win over Ipswich
items.summary: Not since the emergence of a certain Harry Kane has there been this much excitement about a player from Tottenham’s academy. On his first senior start, Luca Williams-Barnett showed just why as the 18-year-old became their youngest Premier League goalscorer since Gareth Bale in 2007 before teeing up Dominic Solanke with a mesmerising and match-winning assist against Ipswich.That made it four league victories from their last five matches for Roberto De Zerbi’s side and the Italian could only have enjoyed the view from the stands as he served his one-match touchline ban. Tottenham have struggled to match their London rivals Arsenal and Chelsea’s record of producing homegrown players in recent years but they appear to have struck gold with Williams-Barnett. Continue reading...

items.title: Newcastle United 2-2 Arsenal: Premier League – as it happened
items.summary: Newcastle roared back to take in a thrilling second half before Noni Madueke’s equaliser earned Arsenal a point“There is an ebb and a flow to Arsenal’s front three, isn’t there?” writes Charles Antaki. “Eze, Havertz, Madueke – in any given game, one will delight and the other two disappoint; one will score and the other two will be all over the place; one will bring joy, and the other two will invite cursing and the gnashing of teeth. And all this is not to mention the chap lurking on the bench. Personally – I admit it – I’d rather have three fully functioning goal machines, but there we are.”We hate it when our teams become successful.He’s prepared emotionally; he knows to accept. We have to be very dominant emotionally to attack Newcastle in the way we want, and he’s ready to do that. Continue reading...

items.title: Fair-weather Silicon Valley pivots away from the right after blue wave: ‘I’m not Maga’
items.summary: From Elon Musk to Palantir’s Alex Karp, CEOs are softening hardline stances in expectation of an influx of DemocratsA short two years ago, Elon Musk stood before an audience of tens of thousands of people in New York City and proudly told them: “I’m not just Maga. I’m dark, gothic Maga.”On Wednesday, Musk spoke with much less conviction. “I’m not Maga,” he said. “Well, at least I’m not sure what Maga means.” The richest person in the world added he felt “foolish” for spending some $500m to elect Republicans in the midterms. “If I could rewind the clock, I would have spent less money,” he said at the New York Times’ DealBook conference, adding that he did not have “some sort of blind adherence to a set of policies by the Republican party”.
